artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ and let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, with sign character $\varepsilon_w=(-1)^{\ell(w)}$, where $\ell(w)$ is the number of inversions of $w\in S_n$. Let $\delta=(n-1,n-2,\dots,1,0)$. For a partition $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$ (with parts allowed to be $0$), let $h_\alpha=h_{\alpha_1}h_{\alpha_2}\cdots h_{\alpha_n}$, where $h_m$ denotes the $m$-th complete homogeneous symmetric function ($h_0=1$ and $h_m=0$ for $m<0$). For partitions $\lambda,\mu$ of length at most $n$ with $\mu\subseteq\lambda$, and an integer $k$ with $0\le k\le \binom{n}{2}$, define the symmetric function
$$
t_{\lambda/\mu,\,k} \;=\; (-1)^{k}\sum_{\substack{w\in S_n\\ \ell(w)\ge k}} \varepsilon_w\, h_{\lambda+\delta - w(\mu+\delta)}.
$$
(For $k=0$ this is the Jacobi–Trudi expansion of the skew Schur function $s_{\lambda/\mu}$; in general $t_{\lambda/\mu,k}$ is a truncation thereof.) Let $\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle$ denote the Hall inner product on symmetric functions, with respect to which the Schur basis $\{s_\nu\}$ is orthonormal.

Problem. Provide a combinatorial interpretation of the scalar product
$$
\big\langle\, t_{\lambda/\mu,\,k},\; s_\nu \,\big\rangle
$$
as $\nu$ ranges over partitions, i.e., a description (e.g. as the cardinality of an explicit family of combinatorial objects, or as a signed/weighted enumeration with a manifestly non-negative interpretation) of the coefficient of $s_\nu$ in the Schur expansion of $t_{\lambda/\mu,k}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question (Stanley, Enumerative Combinatorics vol. 2, Exercise 7.38(b)) asks for a combinatorial interpretation of the Schur coefficients of the truncated Jacobi–Trudi symmetric functions. Recent work (e.g. on Jacobi–Trudi identities via the BGG category O) interprets these coefficients as tensor product multiplicities and establishes Schur positivity, but a manifestly combinatorial interpretation appears not to be known, and the problem is still listed as open in current literature.

status_evidence.title: Revisiting Jacobi–Trudi identities via the BGG category O
status_evidence.snippet: Coefficients in the Schur polynomial expansions of these Jacobi–Trudi truncations have been interpreted as tensor product multiplicities in the BGG category O; combinatorial interpretation remains a stated open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Schur positivity is established representation-theoretically, but a combinatorial interpretation is left open.
